title: Exact empty-selection recovery fixtures
notes: These are manually authored design fixtures, not exported application state.
recordId is a stable human-readable fixture field. Internal __ID is each row zero-based source index, as initializeData assigns.
Expected memberships list recordId in source order. Every expectation includes an exact count.
Only {$fixtureValue:undefined|NaN|Infinity|-Infinity|-0} encodes non-JSON JavaScript datum values; it is fixture transport, not product saved JSON.
Target context:<chart> omits that owner selection, applies workspace/other linked selections and that chart localFilters.
Target selected:<chart> further applies its owner selection, including in notebook localSelections mode.
Target rows includes workspace intersection then Rows filters/search. Target table:<chart> includes table context then own filters/search.

Default removable unit is one stored Filter occurrence; numeric/date intervals and value OR-sets stay intact. Complete chart-selection clearing is an explicit grouped action whose N restrictions are shown.
reasonProbe defines proposed classification contracts; no chart renderer or live UI is exercised.

fixtures.title: Stored boundless and empty-string restrictions remain effective

previews.label: Remove boundless numeric range; retain valid-date and string conditions
Remove boundless date range; retain finite-numeric and string conditions
Remove empty text contains; retain finite-numeric and valid-date conditions

behavior: Recovery inventory must inspect stored restrictions and effective semantics; display-only active-filter heuristics cannot define its inventory.
A boundless numeric range still requires finite numeric values. A boundless date range still requires a valid timestamp. Text contains an empty string still requires a string.
Numeric zero and one are valid millisecond timestamps; string zero is not a date in the baseline parser.

fixtures.title: A valid range pair must survive an individually non-monotone removal

previews.label: Remove latest range alone exposes the older range
Remove both ranges together; preserve category A

behavior: The pair is evaluated against one clone with both original-index occurrences removed together.
Pair search must not discard a unit merely because its single-removal transition is non-monotone.
The joint transition is a valid relaxation and preserves the category restriction; clearing the whole chart would incorrectly admit G3.
